fit: Animal movement model and distinct cited historical human observation
assessment: The article studies movement abnormalities in a mouse model. Its introduction separately recounts a previously published human case of acute illness with visual hallucinations and parkinsonian features, attributed to Richter and colleagues. The human observation is a citation in the background. It adds no independently observed Parkinson cases, food exposure or visual episode rate to the animal paper.

fit: Acute delirium and Parkinson medication differential review
assessment: Lloyd describes visual hallucinations in severe delirium and distinguishes symptoms arising during Parkinson therapy from symptoms attributable to disease. This is clinical diagnostic context. No separate visual episode rate or dried-fig comparison is reported.

fit: Clinical differential review, prior comparison of visual histories
assessment: Quinn describes visual hallucination history in diffuse Lewy body disease. The review also cites a comparison in which visual hallucinations and fluctuations were as common in pure Alzheimer disease, qualifying how specifically those symptoms distinguished diagnoses in the cited evidence. The source supplies diagnostic history without a new patient sample, a visual episode-frequency measure or dried-fig exposure.

fit: Parkinson treatment review, separate visual phenotypes and motor effects
assessment: Quinn distinguishes visual illusions, perceived presence, experiences with retained insight, and visual hallucinations. The review discusses psychotic symptoms during motor off periods and dietary protein in the context of levodopa response and motor fluctuations. The dietary discussion supplies no evidence for dried figs or a visual episode-rate comparison.

fit: Vascular and Lewy body dementia differential review
assessment: Amar and Wilcock contrast vascular dementia with other dementias, including dementia with Lewy bodies and Parkinson disease dementia. The diagnostic box uses early prominent visual hallucinations as one contextual feature. The review reports no new symptom-frequency or dried-fig comparison.

fit: Parkinson apomorphine motor comparison, adverse-event texts pending
assessment: Colzi and colleagues followed 19 people with Parkinson disease and severe motor fluctuations. The abstract reports changes in dyskinesia and time spent off. Its frequency result refers to dyskinesia. Visual hallucination reporting in the complete follow-up remains unresolved.

fit: Visual hallucination case, final diagnosis and main body pending
assessment: The case conference concerns an older patient with behavioral changes and visual hallucinations. The accessible primary opening and bibliographic data identify the case, with final diagnosis and timing details still open. The record supplies no verified dietary comparison.

fit: Four Parkinson patients, open apomorphine challenge, proxy outcomes
assessment: Contrast sensitivity improved and attention performance worsened during the challenge. The authors explicitly did not score the infrequent visual events in the short observation. No dried-fig exposure.
